Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 82, verses 6–9:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿O man, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?﴾ He addressed with this those who denied the Resurrection. Ibn 'Abbas said: "al-insan" (the man) here refers to al-Walid ibn al-Mughira. 'Ikrimah said: Ubayy ibn Khalaf. It was also said: it was revealed concerning Abu al-Ashadd ibn Kaladah al-Jumahi. Also from Ibn 'Abbas: "What has deceived you" means: what was it that deceived you until you disbelieved? "Concerning your Lord, the Generous" means: the One who overlooks [your faults]. Qatadah said: his accursed devil, who was empowered over him, deceived him. Al-Hasan said: his wicked devil deceived him. It was also said: his foolishness and ignorance. This was narrated by al-Hasan from 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him. Ghalib al-Hanafi narrated that he said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited, "O man, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?" [al-Infitar: 6], he said: "Ignorance deceived him." Salih ibn Mismar said: We have been informed that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited, "O man, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?" and said: "His ignorance deceived him." 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: as Allah the Exalted said, "Indeed, he was a wrongdoer, ignorant" [al-Ahzab: 72]. It was also said: the pardon of Allah deceived him, since He did not punish him at the first instance. Ibrahim ibn al-Ash'ath said: It was said to al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad: If Allah were to make you stand before Him on the Day of Resurrection and say to you, "What has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?" [al-Infitar: 6], what would you say? He said: I would say, "Your lowered veils deceived me, for the Generous is the Concealer." Ibn al-Sammak versified it, saying:

O concealer of sin, are you not ashamed,
while Allah is your second in private?
Your Lord's respite to you deceived you,
and His covering of your evil deeds for so long.

Dhu al-Nun al-Misri said: How many a deceived person is under cover while he does not perceive it. Abu Bakr ibn Tahir al-Abhari recited:

The one who is secure has exceeded in self-admiration and arrogance,
and his prolonged persistence has deceived him.
Allah granted you respite, so you defied Him,
and you did not fear the consequence of your sins.

It is narrated from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that he called out to a slave of his several times, but he did not answer. He looked and found him at the door, and said: "Why did you not answer me?" He said: "Because of my trust in your forbearance and my security from your punishment." He admired his answer and freed him. And some people say: "What has deceived you" means: what deceived you and made it seem attractive to you, until you neglected what was obligatory upon you? Ibn Mas'ud said: There is none among you but Allah will speak with him privately on the Day of Resurrection, and He will say to him: "O son of Adam, what deceived you concerning Me? O son of Adam, what did you do with what you knew? O son of Adam, how did you respond to the messengers?"

﴿Who created you﴾ — that is, decreed your creation from a drop [of semen]; ﴿and proportioned you﴾ — in your mother's womb, and made for you two hands, two feet, two eyes, and the rest of your limbs; ﴿and made you balanced﴾ — that is, made you upright and sound in form, as one says, "This is a well-balanced thing" (mu'addal). This is the reading of the common people, and it is the preference of Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim. Al-Farra' and Abu 'Ubayd said: What indicates it is His saying, the Exalted: "Certainly We created man in the best of stature" [al-Tin: 4]. The Kufans — 'Asim, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i — read "fa-'adalaka" with a light (unemphatic) 'ayn, meaning: He inclined you and turned you into whatever form He willed, either beautiful or ugly, either tall or short. And Musa ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Rabah al-Lakhmi narrated from his father, from his grandfather [[The addition is from the tafsir of al-Tha'labi, al-Tabari and al-Durr al-Manthur. The hadith, as narrated by al-Tha'labi after the chain: The Prophet ﷺ said to his grandfather: "What has been born to you?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, what could be born to me? Either a boy or a girl." He said: "Then whom does it resemble?" He said: "It resembles either his mother or his father." Then the Prophet ﷺ said:]]: He said: The Prophet ﷺ said to me: "Indeed, when the drop settles in the womb, Allah brings forth before it every lineage between it and Adam." Have you not read this verse: ﴿in whatever form He willed, He fashioned you﴾ — (meaning) "among what lies between you and Adam." [And 'Ikrimah and Abu Salih said: "in whatever form He willed, He fashioned you" means: if He wills, in the form of a human; and if He wills, in the form of a donkey; and if He wills, in the form of a monkey; and if He wills, in the form of a pig.] Makhul said: if He wills, male, and if He wills, female. Mujahid said: "in whatever form" means: in whatever resemblance, of a father, or a mother, or an uncle, or a maternal uncle, or others. The phrase "fi" (in) is connected to "rakkabaka" (fashioned you), and is not connected to "fa-'adalaka" according to the reading of the one who reads it lightly, because you say "'adaltu ila kadha" (I inclined to such-and-such), and you do not say "'adaltu fi kadha." For this reason al-Farra' rejected the light reading, since he assigned "fi" to "fa-'adalaka." The "ma" may be a superfluous emphatic particle, meaning: in whatever form He willed, He fashioned you. It may also be conditional, meaning: if He willed, He fashioned you in a form other than the human form, such as the form of a monkey, a donkey, or a pig; so "ma" carries the meaning of the condition and the consequent, meaning: in whatever form He wills to fashion you, He fashions you.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Nay! Rather, you deny the Religion﴾ — "kalla" may mean "truly" and "alla" (indeed), so a sentence begins with it. It may also mean "la" (no), with the meaning: the matter is not as you say, that you are correct in your worship of other than Allah. What indicates this is His saying, the Exalted: "What has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?" [al-Infitar: 6]. Likewise al-Farra' says: the meaning becomes: "It is not as you have been deceived by Him." It was also said: meaning, the matter is not as you say, that there is no resurrection. It was also said: it carries the sense of prohibition and deterrence, i.e., do not be deceived by Allah's forbearance and generosity, so that you abandon reflection upon His signs. Ibn al-Anbari said: The good pause is at "bi-l-din" and at "rakkabaka," and pausing at "kalla" is ugly. "Bal tukadhdhibuna" — O people of Makkah, you deny the Religion, that is, the Reckoning. "Bal" serves to negate something preceding and affirm something else. Their denial of the Resurrection was well known, even though no mention of it has occurred in this surah.

**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on Surah 82, verses 10–12:**

God's words: ﴿And indeed, over you are guardians﴾, meaning watchers from among the angels, ﴿noble (kiraman)﴾, meaning honoured by God, as in His words: ﴿noble and dutiful scribes﴾ [Abasa: 16]. Here there are three issues.

The first: It is related from the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "Honour the noble scribes, who do not leave you except in two situations: when one relieves oneself (al-khara'a), or during sexual intercourse (al-jima'). So when one of you bathes, let him conceal himself behind a wall [the addition from al-Durr al-Manthur, where it is found: the occasion of this hadith was that he (peace be upon him) saw a man bathing in an open desert ... etc.] or behind something else, or let his brother conceal him." It is related from Ali (may God be pleased with him) that he said: "The angel does not cease to turn away from the servant as long as he is uncovered (badi al-'awra)." And it is related: "When the servant enters the bathhouse (al-hammam) without a loincloth, his two angels curse him."

The second: People have differed regarding the disbelievers: do they have guardian angels or not? Some said: No, because their state is evident and their deeds are uniform; God, the Exalted, says: ﴿The guilty will be known by their marks﴾ [al-Rahman: 41]. It was also said: Rather, they do have guardians, based on God's words: ﴿No! Rather, you deny the Judgment. And indeed, over you are guardians, noble, recording, who know what you do﴾ [al-Infitar: 9–12]. And He said: ﴿As for him who is given his record in his left hand﴾ [al-Haqqa: 25], and He said: ﴿As for him who is given his record behind his back﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 10]. Thus He informed that the disbelievers will have a record, and that there will be guardians over them. If it is said: What does the one on the right write, when he has no good deed? It is said to him: The one who writes on the left works under the permission of his companion, and he serves as a witness to that, even if he does not write. And God knows best.

The third: Sufyan was asked: How do the angels know that the servant has intended a good deed or an evil deed? He said: When the servant intends a good deed, they find from him the scent of musk, and when he intends an evil deed, they find from him the stench of rot. This has already been discussed in (Surah) Qaf, under His words: ﴿Not a word does he utter but that there is with him a watcher, ready﴾ [Qaf: 18], giving further explanation of the meaning of this verse. The scholars have disliked speaking while relieving oneself (al-gha'it) and during intercourse, because the angel departs from the servant at those times. This matter was also discussed at the end of (Surah) Al 'Imran. And it is related from al-Hasan: "They know; nothing of your deeds is hidden from them." It was also said: "They know what appears from you, not what you speak to yourselves." And God knows best.
